title: Fracture Undulation Modelling in Discontinuum Analysis: Implications for Rock Mass Strength Assessment
content: Synthetic rock mass (SRM) models are an invaluable component of rock engineering. Thus far, joints are implicitly modelled by adjusting rock mass properties, while flat joints are adopted for discontinuum models. This paper does not question the fundamental validity of these well-established methods for characterizing discontinuity shear strength under controlled laboratory conditions. The implicit assumption underlying this application is that surface undulation has a negligible impact on rock mass interlocking mechanisms and, consequently, on overall modelled rock mass strength. Compelling evidence suggests this assumption requires careful reconsideration. The difference in rock mass behaviour between explicitly undulated models and flat joints did not appear to exhibit any consistent patterns. Rough and flat joints did not, in the findings of this article, result in any consistent rock mass peak strength. Therefore, engineers may ascertain rock mass behaviour and strength without the use of explicit rock fracture undulations.
